examples.instruction: Rewrite to be more active and less wordy: 'It was decided by the team that the deployment of the new system should be completed by the end of the month.'
examples.thinking: Find the hidden verbs ('decision' -> decide, 'deployment' -> deploy), kill passives, drop filler. Name the agent, give the concrete deadline. One clause should be enough.
examples.response: The team will deploy the new system by month-end.

examples.instruction: What makes writing sound like it was written by an AI, and how do I avoid it?
examples.thinking: The tells are mechanical rhythm: stacked hedges, walls of em-dashes, jargon verbs, always-three-part lists, and a grand-closing platitude. Fixes: cut the first and last sentence of a draft, kill the hedges, let one concrete detail carry the paragraph.
examples.response: The tells are mechanical rhythm: hedged verbose phrasing, em-dash walls, jargon verbs, three-part lists, and a closing platitude. Strip the first and last sentence of any draft, kill every hedge, and give one concrete detail instead of a summary.
